why_next: The oracle-guided encode-agnostic decode experiment resolved the parent FALSIFIES (60/240) to 240/240 on all CDN conditions, proving CDN re-encoding is losslessly recoverable. However, two blocking gaps remain for product readiness: (1) the oracle (ground_truth_sha256) is circular — product cannot use it; greedy decode without oracle is highly likely to work (format headers are distinct) but unmeasured; (2) zero CDN cache HIT responses were observed (all DYNAMIC) — stale serving could deliver different bytes. Both gaps are small, discriminating tests with high information gain. The oracle-free test directly converts a lossless-recovery observation into a deployable mechanism. The HIT test closes the last untested CDN path. Together they determine whether C-MEAS-VALID advances to VALIDATED or remains EXPERIMENTAL.

established: Encoding-agnostic ORACLE-GUIDED iterative decompression (try brotli→gzip→identity until SHA256 matches ground truth) losslessly recovers ground truth for ALL tested Cloudflare free-tier CDN transformations on DYNAMIC responses: 240/240 primary cells (48 cells × 5 reps), 80/80 BINARY, 15/15 identity, 45/45 depth 3-5 (100%, threshold ≥80%), 30/30 large payloads >100KB (100%, threshold ≥80%). Parent FALSIFIES (60/240) fully resolved. Positive control B-LOCALHOST-DIRECT 240/240, null control B-CDN-IDENTITY 15/15. Fixed-order regression 60/240 replicates parent. Audit PASS confirms recomputed metrics match producer on deduped data (576 unique URLs). (EXP-RUNTIME-35542474231, audit REVISE with ceiling bounded)

CDN does not corrupt bytes — the parent's fixed-origin-order failure was in the framing assumption (replaying origin's layer stack), not data integrity. CDN Accept-Encoding negotiation transforms are lossless: gunzip, de-brotli, silent re-encode, identity text gzip-compress — all recoverable by iterative decode. (EXP-RUNTIME-35538865067 forensic + EXP-RUNTIME-35542474231 frozen validation)

unknown: Does oracle-free greedy iterative decompression (no SHA256 check) achieve 240/240 byte-identical correctness on the same 48-cell Cloudflare CDN matrix? Highly likely (format headers are distinct: brotli 0xCEB2CF81, gzip 0x1F8B) but unmeasured. Audit V4 confirms method distribution shows each cell requires a deterministic path.

Does encoding-agnostic decode recover correctness for CDN cache HIT (stale) responses? All 423 CDN responses in this experiment were cf-cache-status=DYNAMIC; zero HIT observed. Stale-cache serving could deliver different bytes.

Does encoding-agnostic decode work for other CDN providers (Fastly, Akamai, CloudFront), paid tiers, other geographic edges, HTTP/2 or H3, concurrent clients, or mixed chunk-size pipelines? Explicitly not tested.
What is the amortized latency/cost of iterative try-brotli-then-gzip versus fixed-order decode? Not measured.

Do CDN re-encodings at deeper depths (3-5) with different quality/level settings ever produce ambiguous bytes where both brotli and gzip decompress successfully (oracle tie-break needed)? Not observed but not falsified.
Were depth 3-5 and large-payload CDN deliveries also DYNAMIC? Yes per deduped rows — but HIT path remains untested.

If 240/240 byte-identical to ground truth, the deployable decoder is validated.
